ov: The biggest cat in the Americas and the only one of the roaring big cats native there. A stocky, heavily spotted hunter that sticks close to rivers and swamps.

why.ac: Varies by region: largely active by day in parts of the Amazon and the Pantanal, and mainly by night in the Atlantic Forest.
why.dg: Attacks on people are rare, and most happened when a jaguar was cornered or wounded.

rg: From Mexico through Central America to northern Argentina, with strongholds in the Amazon basin and the Pantanal wetlands.
df: Broad: capybara, peccaries and deer, but also caimans, turtles and fish, especially in the Pantanal.

cf.tip: Leopards are slimmer, with smaller, empty rosettes, and live in Africa and Asia. In the Americas, a big spotted cat is a jaguar.
An adult cougar has a plain tawny coat with no spots at all.
